parts.title: Notices and messages
parts.instructions: For each notice, choose what it means.
notices: CAR PARK: The car park is full on Saturdays after eleven o'clock. Please use the park-and-ride bus from the edge of town. Tickets cost two pounds.

DRIVING LESSONS: Learn with a friendly teacher. The first lesson is half price. Cars have two sets of pedals for extra safety.

Magnus drives a long way to work each day. He wants a car that uses very little fuel and is cheap to run.

parts.title: Passing my driving test
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I took my driving test three times before I passed. The first time, I was so nervous that I forgot to look in my mirror before pulling away from the kerb. The examiner, a serious man with a clipboard, wrote something down immediately. I knew that I had failed after only two minutes.

The second time, I made a different mistake. I was driving along a quiet road when I saw a dog running across it. I stopped suddenly, and the car behind me almost hit mine. Again, I failed, although the examiner told me that I had stopped for a good reason.

After that, I took extra lessons with a new teacher, a calm lady called Hilda. She taught me to breathe slowly and to treat the test like a normal drive. She also made me practise in different kinds of weather, including heavy rain.

On the third attempt, it was raining hard, but I felt oddly relaxed. I drove carefully, checked all my mirrors, and even smiled at the examiner. When he told me that I had passed, I could not speak. I called my mother immediately and cried for five minutes.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer fail the first test?
options: He forgot to check his mirror
He drove through a red light
He hit another car in the street
questions.explanation: He forgot to look in his mirror before pulling away.

questions.prompt: What happened during the second test?
options: A dog ran across the road
He got lost in the old town
questions.explanation: He saw a dog running across the road and stopped suddenly.

questions.prompt: How did Hilda help the writer?
options: She lent him her own small car
She taught him to stay calm
She spoke to the examiner for him
questions.explanation: She taught him to breathe slowly and treat the test like a normal drive.

questions.prompt: What was the weather like for the third test?
options: It was foggy and rather cold
It was bright and very sunny
questions.explanation: It was raining hard.

questions.prompt: How did the writer react to passing?
options: He thanked the examiner very loudly
He telephoned his mother in tears
questions.explanation: He called his mother and cried for five minutes.

parts.title: The history of the car
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
The first cars appeared more than a hundred and thirty years ago, and they were very different from the ones we know today. [1] They were slow, noisy and often broke down, and in many places, people were afraid of them.

In the beginning, only rich people could afford a car. [2] Everything changed in the early twentieth century, when an American businessman began to build cars on a moving line in his factory.

This made cars much cheaper, so ordinary families could buy them. [3] Soon, roads were built all over the country, and petrol stations appeared in every town.

Today there are more than a billion cars in the world. [4] Many experts believe that most cars will run on electricity within twenty years. [5] Whatever happens, it seems clear that the car will remain an important part of life.
sentences: Many drivers now think about the damage that they cause to the air.
Each one had to be made by hand, which took weeks.
Some of them looked more like carriages without horses.
People could travel further and more quickly than ever before.
The best way to learn to drive is with a good teacher.
The future may bring cars that drive themselves.

gaps.explanation: Carriages without horses describes how different the first cars looked, and "they were slow" follows.
Each car made by hand explains why only rich people could afford one.
The cheaper cars meant people could travel further, and then roads were built.
Damage to the air links to the billion cars and to electric cars.
Cars that drive themselves is a future thought leading to the concluding sentence.

parts.title: A message about a lift
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Hi Peter, Thank you for offering [1] give me a lift to the station tomorrow. My train [2] at half past seven, so I need to leave the house at seven. Do not worry if you [3] late, as I can walk fast. I have [4] my suitcase, and it is really heavy. I will pay [5] the petrol, of course. It is very kind [6] you!

questions.prompt: Gap 2

questions.prompt: Gap 5

parts.title: Road safety
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Every year, many people are hurt in road accidents, and most of them could be avoided. The most important rule is to wear a seat belt [1] you travel by car, even on a short journey. Drivers should never use a phone [2] driving, because it takes attention away from the road. They should also never drive if they are tired. Children under twelve must sit [3] the back seat. Remember that it takes longer to stop when the road is wet, so drive more slowly [4] rain. If you cross the road on foot, always look both ways [5] you start. These rules are easy to follow, and they could save [6] life.

gaps.explanation: Wear a seat belt "when" you travel.

parts.title: A talk about learning to drive
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: reginald
turns.text: Good evening, everybody. I'm Reginald, and I run the Safe Drive school. Today I'd like to tell you how our courses work. You can start learning when you are seventeen. Most people need about forty lessons, and each one lasts an hour. We usually recommend two lessons a week. The price for each lesson is thirty pounds, but we offer a discount if you pay for ten at once. Our cars are blue, with the school name on the doors. Before the practical test, you must pass a theory test on a computer, which has fifty questions. You need to answer at least forty-three correctly. Our office is open from nine until six, and you can book lessons by phone or online.

gaps.prompt: You can start learning at the age of ___
gaps.explanation: You can start when you are seventeen.
Most people need about forty lessons.
The theory test has fifty questions.

parts.title: A taxi driver
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: bertram
turns.text: Today's guest is Kezia Adams, who has been a taxi driver in this city for twenty years. Kezia, why did you choose this job?

turns.speaker: kezia
turns.text: I used to work in an office, and I hated sitting still all day. I love driving, and I love meeting new people.

turns.speaker: bertram
turns.text: What is a typical day like?

turns.speaker: kezia
turns.text: I start at six in the morning, taking people to the station. Then I drive shoppers, tourists and sometimes children to school.

turns.speaker: bertram
turns.text: Who is your most memorable passenger?

turns.speaker: kezia
turns.text: A famous singer. She sang in the back seat all the way to the airport, and I didn't recognise her until she got out!

turns.speaker: bertram
turns.text: Have you ever had a problem with a passenger?

turns.speaker: kezia
turns.text: Rarely. Once a man left without paying, so I followed him. He was very embarrassed and gave me double.

turns.speaker: bertram
turns.text: What do you find most difficult about the work?

turns.speaker: kezia
turns.text: Sitting in traffic. On a wet Friday evening, it can take an hour to go three kilometres.

turns.speaker: bertram
turns.text: Do you think driverless taxis will replace you?

turns.speaker: kezia
turns.text: Maybe one day, but I'm not worried. People like to chat, and a computer can't tell you where the best café is.

questions.explanation: She hated sitting still in an office and loves driving.

questions.explanation: She starts at six in the morning.
